title: Probabilistic traffic prober for canary and shadow validation with adaptive early-stop
creator: Arianna Chen
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, probabilistic traffic prober as a first-class option for model version experiments. The prober will send short-lived probabilistic samples of live traffic to candidate model variants (canaries) and optionally mirror full requests to shadow variants for offline validation. It must provide adaptive early-stop logic using online statistical tests and integrate with Redwood Console for visibility and automated rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Config schema exposes per-experiment: probe_rate (0.0-1.0), shadow_mirror boolean, primary_metrics list, safety_budget (max tolerated divergence), and stat_test config (type, alpha, drift_window)
Probe runner implemented in serving layer that samples requests according to probe_rate and routes them to target model variant without increasing overall primary traffic fraction
Online statistical checks supported: sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) and a simple Bayesian posterior check over selected metrics
Adaptive early-stop: if test crosses preconfigured thresholds before scheduled exposure, system pauses rollout and triggers alert + optional auto-rollback
Shadow validation pipeline stores mirrored responses, links to Console evaluation workspace, and supports configurable retention for privacy
Console shows per-probe metrics: sample count, metric drift, p-values/odds, expected time-to-decision, and active safety budget consumption
Integration tests simulate bursty traffic and ensure probe_rate does not amplify latency or resource contention beyond thresholds
implementation_notes: Probe decision happens at routing layer; it should use consistent hashing so probe users are uniformly distributed across cohorts
SPRT chosen as default for fast detection with bounded error rates; Bayesian check used as secondary signal with configurable priors

Safety budget uses an exponential decay to allow recovery over time instead of permanent locks; safety_budget specified as percentage of tolerated metric degradation (e.g., +2% latency or -1% quality)
Shadow mirror must redact PII and respect retention/KMS policies (hook to Private deploy KMS integration for on-prem customers)
We must avoid mixing probe sampling with user-visible rate limits; probes should be accounted separately in billing and console quotas
Rollbacks: automated rollback requires two independent signals or a single high-severity crossing depending on customer tier (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
Runtime will expose a lightweight metrics stream for prober decisions so Console can surface near-real-time leaderboards
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal dogfood): probe_rate=0.01, shadow_mirror=false, run 1 week against low-priority cohort. Observe resource usage and test false positive rate.
Phase 2 (beta customers): add shadow_mirror=true for consenting customers, probe_rate up to 0.05, enable SPRT with alpha=0.05, safety_budget=2% for latency.
Phase 3 (general availability): full Console UI, config API, auto-rollback gates, and documentation. Default probe_rate remains conservative (0.01) but configurable per-experiment.
Fallback and kill-switch: immediate global toggle with audit log; per-customer kill-switch for Private deployments
monitoring_and_alerts: Primary alert: 'Prober safety_budget_exceeded' when observed metric delta exceeds safety_budget for configured consecutive windows
Secondary alert: 'Prober-high-p_value' when tests reach p>0.95 for regression hypothesis indicating probable degradation
Telemetry: sample count, average latency, 95th latency, loss-of-quality metric (task-specific), SPRT odds ratio, Bayesian posterior mean/CI
Dashboard: experiment timeline, decision boundary chart, cohort breakdown, and request/response examples (redacted)
api_changes: POST /experiments - new fields: probe_rate, shadow_mirror, safety_budget, stat_test (type, params)
GET /experiments/:id/prober_status - returns online stats, current verdict, and sample counts
Events: experiment.decision (pause/continue/rollback) emitted to webhook and to Console activity feed
privacy_considerations: Mirrored payloads are redacted using existing PII rules before persisting to S3/backing store
Retention defaults to 7 days for probe traces; configurable per-tenant with max 90 days
Private deployments must honor on-prem retention and cannot send mirrored payloads to Redwood-managed analytics without explicit opt-in
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: probes skew upstream cache hit ratios and latency. Mitigation: use header hints to bypass caches where appropriate and validate in integration tests
Risk: frequent early-stop churn creates oscillation. Mitigation: add cooldown period and require monotonic worsening across windows before auto-rollback
Risk: underpowered statistical tests on low-traffic endpoints. Mitigation: fall back to extended observation windows and mark as 'insufficient data' in Console
